title: Why is the Star Formation Rate Proportional to Dense Gas Mass?
question: Why is the star formation rate linearly proportional to the dense molecular gas mass (the Gao-Solomon relation), and can this proportionality be explained by deterministic relationships between the gravitationally bound gas mass, the mass of the most massive core, the mass of the most massive star, and the star formation rate?

recipe.goal: Derive molecular hydrogen column density (N_H2) maps for nearby and distant clouds from Herschel data
recipe.method: Convolve Herschel 5-band images (70, 160, 250, 350, 500 um) to a common 36.9'' resolution, regrid to 4.0'' pixel size, and perform pixelwise single-component modified black-body SED fitting.
assumptions: Dust opacity kappa_nu = 1.0(nu/230 GHz)^beta cm^2 g^-1, dust emissivity index beta = 1.8, gas-to-dust mass ratio R = 100, mean molecular weight mu = 2.8, scattering opacity ignored.

recipe.goal: Measure parental gravitationally bound gas mass (M_gas^bound) from N-PDFs
recipe.method: Set an optimal column density cutoff (N_cut) based on sensitivity, map area, and last closed contour; fit the N-PDF with a log-normal plus power-law function to find the transitional column density (N_threshold), and integrate the mass above N_threshold.
key_parameters: Cloud-specific N_cut values (0.28 to 3.55 x 10^21 cm^-2 for nearby clouds; 6.3 to 19.9 x 10^21 cm^-2 for distant clouds)
assumptions: Power-law tail of the N-PDF above N_threshold traces self-gravitating, gravitationally bound gas.

recipe.goal: Extract dense cores and derive the mass of the most massive core (M_core^max)
recipe.method: Smooth nearby cloud N_H2 maps and distant cloud ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm free-free subtracted continuum maps to a consistent 0.03 pc spatial resolution; subtract background using a 256-pixel box; extract cores with SExtractor; compute core masses by summing N_H2 pixels for nearby clouds or applying gray-body dust emission equation for distant clouds.
key_parameters: Spatial resolution = 0.03 pc; background box = 256 pixels; nthresh = 3; deblend_nthresh = 512; deblend_cont = 10^-5; min_npix = number of pixels in a Herschel or ALMA beam; deconvolution factor eta = 2.4
assumptions: Mean molecular weight mu = 2.8; for distant clouds: specific dust opacity at 1.3 mm kappa_1.3mm = 0.01 cm^2 g^-1 (beta = 1.8), uniform dust temperature T_dust = 100 K (or 300 K for W51-E, W51-IRS2, and G327.29 in fiducial Method Two).

recipe.goal: Determine the scaling relation between M_core^max and M_gas^bound and connect it to the Gao-Solomon SFR relation
recipe.method: Perform linear regression in log-log space between M_core^max and M_gas^bound for the 23 clouds (and excluding 4 outliers with missing flux); combine with SFE = 30% and the theoretical SFR-m_star^max relation from Yan et al. (2017) to infer SFR^theory and compare with the Gao-Solomon relation and observational SFRs.
assumptions: Star-forming efficiency SFE = 30% (m_star^max ~ 0.3 * M_core^max); M_gas^bound approximates M_gas^dense; Gao-Solomon relation scaled upward by factor 2.7.

recipe.goal: Test whether observed M_core^max values are consistent with random (stochastic) sampling of the CMF
recipe.method: Fit the CMF of nearby clouds at the high-mass end; run Monte Carlo simulations drawing n(M > 3 M_sun) cores from a power-law CMF (pool of 10^6 cores) 5000 times per cloud (and 10^6 iterations for Taurus+Perseus combined), comparing simulated M_core^max distributions and scatter to observations.
key_parameters: Low-mass cutoff = 3 M_sun; CMF power-law index Gamma = -1.00 and -1.35; initial pool size = 10^6 cores; 5000 repetitions per cloud; 10^6 iterations for Taurus+Perseus test
assumptions: Largest possible stellar mass m_up = 150 M_sun or 100 M_sun; SFE = 30%; largest probable core mass = m_up / SFE (500 M_sun or 333 M_sun); total core mass in set C cannot exceed SFE * M_gas^bound.

score_reason: The paper uses publicly released, fully reduced archival FITS images (ALMA-IMF Dataverse and HGBS/Hi-GAL archives), states all SExtractor parameters, equations, dust opacities, temperatures, and N-PDF cutoffs in tables, and provides complete output tables for verification. Minor deductions are due to reliance on a custom Orion A map from an earlier paper, unstated cloud boundary definitions for N-PDFs, and details deferred to a submitted companion paper.
rediscovery_reason: All input ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm free-free subtracted continuum images and Herschel maps are publicly downloadable, the core extraction and mass calculation recipes (smoothing to 0.03 pc, SExtractor settings, gray-body equations, and N-PDF thresholds) are explicitly specified, and the main results (core masses, bound gas masses, and power-law slope 0.506) are numeric and tabulated.
